completedTasks.title: Close the books on SearchAsync's phase attribution; make VERSION the only version marker
completedTasks.outcome: Issue #382. The six SearchTimings phases never decomposed a search: SearchAsync opened the bank and embedded the query before the first timer started. Measured on the live bank 2026-08-17 (n=12): memory_search averaged 287.03 ms against 169.12 ms of phases, 41% in no phase; worst recorded search left 1,177.68 of 1,799.91 ms unattributed. Adds search.open and search.embed plus a measured Total recorded as search.total and deliberately kept OUT of PhaseNames (summing PhaseNames stays correct; a derived SeriesNames carries everything). Three findings corrected the issue's own premise: the gate it asked for cannot be built (memory_search is a stopwatch around the whole SDK dispatch, with the access gate, the query guard, a POST-return bank write and serialization outside SearchAsync, so sum-of-phases can never equal it at any granularity -- the phases close against search.total instead, ADR-0080); query embedding is not a bare neural forward pass but four settings reads, a cached ONNX session build, a WordPiece trim, then the pass; and the '~2 bank opens per search' it leaned on is stale, a prefix read made it one. Closure gate uses a real clock with a 28 ms residual budget chosen from measurement -- a cold isolated run has a 13-29 ms residual from JIT and query-plan compile, so the test does a discarded warm-up search first; without it the budget would have been flaky. completedTasks.title: Make table chunking adjudicable: table-bearing corpus, a gate that re-chunks, span-anchored relevance
completedTasks.outcome: Supplies the three things ADR-0077 named as missing, and ships no production change (MarkdownChunker untouched). A table-bearing corpus: 13 documents vendored at pinned commits from ai-badger and arasz-home-page, both external to this repo so no retrieval parameter has ever been swept against them, plus 16 graded queries whose answers are table cells. A gate that re-chunks: TableCorpusBank ingests that markdown at test time through the production FileIngestor rather than reading the committed jsaa bank, proven non-blind by a 128-token re-ingest that takes 343 chunks to 784 and moves 4 of 16 per-query scores. A span-anchored response variable: a chunk is relevant iff it is from the expected document AND carries the graded answer span, so ground truth survives an arm that deletes a chunk id. Baseline: mean nDCG@5 0.070683, mean MRR@10 0.089658 at the production budget, most queries exactly 0, with the answer-bearing chunk only 49% table content on average. Two findings kept rather than smoothed: a reversed top-10 OUTSCORES the real order (0.161 vs 0.071) so reversal is not a valid discriminator here and mispairing is used instead; and a span anchor bounds inflation without freezing it, since the 48-token overlay takes the largest relevance set from 1 to 3 under a 6.2x finer corpus against whole-file relevance growing 5.9x. ADR-0079 records it. completedTasks.title: Direct-HTTP clients can present the loopback token again
completedTasks.summary: ADR-0020's token gate left every non-proxy route unable to authenticate; the Hermes plugin's http transport was one of four surfaces, not the defect. The gate now also accepts Authorization: Bearer (one credential, two envelopes, FixedTimeEquals on both) because `hermes mcp add --url` prompts for authentication by default and can only produce Bearer. serve --mcp-entry prints a headers map with a ${AIRACCOON_MCP_TOKEN} placeholder instead of a bare URL - verified against the installed CLIs that both Hermes and Claude Code expand it, and that an unset variable warns but still sends the literal string, which is why /mcp now renders a distinct 401 for a present-but-wrong credential (an unexpanded placeholder is a present one; the old wording told users to add the header they had just added). The plugin reads token_file, default ~/.ai-raccoon/mcp-token, and attaches it only for loopback URLs. Pre-implementation review caught that the naive default would have shipped the loopback secret to whatever url was configured, and that one 'seen RED' recipe could not fire on any machine that had run ai-raccoon. Post-implementation review caught follow_redirects=True keeping a custom header across origins - a token-exfiltration path the plan's own residual-risk paragraph had reasoned away on a premise a different lane invalidated. QA against a real gated server found the client discarding the server's diagnostic entirely: anyio surfaced the 401 as asyncio.CancelledError, a BaseException with an empty str(), outside the except Exception in both connect() and the provider. 1.6.0.
decisions: ADR-0020:182 asserted `serve --mcp-entry` was unaffected and a direct url entry remained valid. False the day it was written - the token shipped in the same change. That assertion is why nobody re-checked the direct route. Struck and marked as corrected rather than reworded.

The mismatch 401 is scoped to /mcp. ADR-0022 guards /shutdown with the same gate and pins one identical body for absent/wrong/truncated so the refusal cannot say whether a token exists - a tested invariant, not a comment. /mcp is configured by hand and needs the diagnosability; /shutdown's only caller is `serve --restart` reading the token off disk and gains nothing from it.

No WWW-Authenticate on the 401 despite accepting a Bearer envelope. RFC 7235 makes it a MUST, but a bare Bearer challenge may push spec-following clients into an OAuth discovery flow this server does not serve. Recorded as a considered trade-off.
